messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Automated Diagnostics
parts:
I whipped up an example of automated diagnostics that you can try out
at https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstan/tree/feature/automated_diagnostics.
Obviously, having some misbehaving model output files will be handy!
Or just take a look at the logic in the source itself,
https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstan/blob/feature/automated_diagnostics/src/cmdstan/print_diagnostics.cpp.

Any opinions on the text? It’s meant to be informative but make no hard
decision about the validity of the output (as theoretically we cannot do
that). The user will have to have a basic understanding of a Markov
chain — eventually we can reference the appropriate review section
in the manual.

Any diagnostics I’m missing?

For those that use CmdStan, is this best kept as a separate executable
(keeping bin/print agnostic to validity) or should we roll it together into
one single analysis executable?

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Re: Automated Diagnostics
parts:
On Wednesday, April 1, 2015 at 7:46:51 AM UTC-7, Michael Betancourt wrote:
>
> Any opinions on the text? It’s meant to be informative but make no hard
> decision about the validity of the output (as theoretically we cannot do
> that). The user will have to have a basic understanding of a Markov
> chain — eventually we can reference the appropriate review section
> in the manual.

Re divergent iterations message: Maybe also note that this is often better fixed by un-centering (aka Matt tricking) the model. I haven't explored tweaking the sampler much, but I doubt the efficiency gain could approach what comes from a non-centered parameterization. Even without any Cholesky stuff, just moving the scale parameters to the linear model kills most of the divergent iters I've experienced, with the natural huge increase in n_eff/(iter-warmup).

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Automated Diagnostics

The problem is that (non-)centered parameterizations apply to only
hierarchical models and hence the advice doesn’t quite make sense
as a general solution.

If you have an example where bin/print crashes, please file a bug
report with a reproducible example. Of course, there's only so
much size a given program is going to be able to handle. bin/print
has to do an FFT on each column of the output to compute n_eff.

- Bob
